sources.title: Chile signals slow copper recovery from historic output slump
evidence: State copper commission Cochilco cut its 2027 production forecast to 5.08 million metric tons, implying a 3% rebound.
It also slashed this year’s estimate to 4.94 million tons from 5.27 million amid accidents and wild weather
It forecasts a surplus next year equivalent to just 0.8% of consumption, leaving little cushion

sources.title: Italy’s top court upholds shutdown of former Ilva steelworks, in setback to Meloni
evidence: Italy’s Supreme Court upheld a lower court ruling ordering the shutdown of blast furnaces at the former Ilva steelworks
adding uncertainty for the plant and its roughly 8,000 direct employees
She has said Rome has committed around €5 billion ($5.6 billion) to the steelmaker since taking office in 2022.
The company had previously warned that closing the blast furnaces could lead to the permanent shutdown of the plant
The government recently extended the deadline for binding bids to November 9

sources.title: US to impose 50% tariffs on PET imports from Canada on Friday
evidence: The US is on track to impose on Friday tariffs of 50% on imports of polyester from Canada under Section 338.
The US added polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and elastomeric polyurethanes to the imports covered by the new tariffs
The Section 338 tariffs provide no exceptions for imports that comply with the nations’ trade deal
In 2024, Canada exported 71.7 million kg of PET under HTS code 3907.61.00, which was worth nearly $128 million
In 2025, the figures were 64.0 million kg worth nearly $110.6 million

sources.title: Russian refiners ramp up diesel output after US deal, sources say
evidence: Russian refiners are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas
Since Russia’s diesel export ban took effect in August, its oil companies have had to cut production
diesel output in Russia fell in the first half of October to about 160,000 tons per day
After the new export quotas arrived mid-month, production began to rise towards 180,000 tons per day.
That would leave at least 40,000 tons per day, or more than 1 million tons a month, available for export.
